data_quality_notes: July 2026 is the most recent fully closed month as of 2026-08-18. Every value was read directly from the raw InfoSparks CSVs in data/imports/mls_stats/2026-08-17/ (San Clemente column, Residential / Single Family, monthly) and cross-checked against the parsed data/market_stats/2026-07_market_moves.json. Both agree on all eight metrics.

SOURCE REVISION: InfoSparks revised June 2026 San Clemente upward between the 2026-07-24 and 2026-08-17 pulls. Active listings 96 to 102, pending sales 46 to 47, months supply 2.6 to 2.7. The prior snapshot (2026-07_san_clemente_sfr.json) published the pre-revision figures. Immaterial to any published copy, but June-vs-July month-over-month comparisons should use the revised June numbers, not the older file.

Supply is the story this month. Active listings fell to 88, down 45% year over year and down from 102 in June, and months of supply tightened to 2.3 from 3.8 a year ago. This is the tightest San Clemente single-family supply in the tracked series.
Median days active dropped to 9, from 30 a year ago and 11 in June. Median percent of last list price received is 99.0%, up from 98.3% a year ago.

Median sales price of $1,874,950 is essentially flat year over year (+0.5%) and flat against June ($1,892,500 revised). At roughly 48 closings a month, single-month medians move on transaction mix. The durable read is flat-to-slightly-up pricing on sharply tighter supply and much faster absorption.
Pending sales (39) are a flow metric, new pendings originated in July, not homes currently under contract. Up 14.7% year over year but down from 47 in June, which is normal summer seasonality.
market_summary: San Clemente single-family supply tightened hard through July. Active listings (88) are down 45% year over year and months of supply fell to 2.3 from 3.8, the tightest reading in the tracked series, while homes that are priced right are clearing in a median of 9 days at 99.0% of last list. The July median of $1,874,950 is flat year over year, up 0.5%. The market is not being driven by price growth right now. It is being driven by how little there is to buy and how fast the well-priced homes go.
